record.title: No rate limiting: unauthenticated flooding evicts legitimate messages and burns Worker quota
record.description: POST /thread/message in features/groupchat/worker/src/index.js has no rate limit, per-IP/per-token counter, time window, or 429 path: the only bound is MAX_MESSAGES=200 with silent oldest-first eviction. Role=user posts are not turn-limited (turn-taking and the 6-round cap only constrain role=agent, max 12 agent posts per thread), so an unlimited stream of user posts can push seq past 200 and silently drop the oldest messages. Hunter's 200 posts in ~27s reaching seq 213 with seqs 1-13 evicted follows directly from this code; I did not re-flood (thread was reset clean) and verified the code plus the reset live state instead.

trace.what: POST /thread/message handler; only checks are checkToken (line 200), JSON/role validation, thread open, and agent turn-taking (lines 217-224) — no rate, count, window, or per-IP check anywhere in the handler or file.

Every accepted post unconditionally does thread.seq += 1 and thread.messages.push(...); role=user posts never consume a turn and never advance round/max_rounds, so there is no indirect throttle on them.

if (thread.messages.length > MAX_MESSAGES) thread.messages = thread.messages.slice(-MAX_MESSAGES) at lines 233-234, with MAX_MESSAGES=200 at line 65: overflow silently evicts oldest-first with no error, warning, or eviction notice to the caller or relay.

evidence.output: Only hit is line 55 comment: 'hundred requests/day of the 100,000/day free quota.' No rate/throttle/429/counter code. MAX_MESSAGES=200 (line 65); slice(-MAX_MESSAGES) at line 234.

HTTP 200: {"id":"groupchat-mwguv0lq","topic":"","status":"open","round":1,"max_rounds":6,"next_agent":"default","seq":0,"updated_at":"2026-11-14T20:25:39.278Z","messages":[]} — confirms reset clean (seq 0, 0 messages); no posts made.

HTTP 200: {"service":"qwenpaw-groupchat","store":"durable-object (sqlite)","auth_required":false,...} — token still NOT set live, so the flood path is currently unauthenticated (same precondition as groupchat-open-thread).

record.conditions: INDEPENDENT finding — do not fold into groupchat-open-thread. Setting GROUPCHAT_TOKEN fixes unauthenticated posting but does not fix this: a token holder (relay, user, or anyone the token leaks to) can still flood, and quota burn / silent eviction are availability impacts distinct from merely posting a bogus message. Severity DOWNGRADED medium -> low: 200 posts is trivial against the 100,000 req/day Free quota stated in the file header (at the hunter's ~7.4 req/s, ~100k requests would take ~3.7h of sustained flooding); eviction affects only this one auxiliary thread, agent posts are already turn/round-limited, user posts do not inject into QwenPaw directly, and no data beyond thread history is lost. Do not double-count the currently-open (auth_required:false) state — that part belongs to groupchat-open-thread. Confidence is medium, not high, because the 200-posts/27s flood itself was not re-run by design (thread reset clean, do not re-pollute); the no-rate-limit code path and the eviction sink were verified directly from source.
record.remediation: Add an in-Worker per-IP (and per-author) counter in the Durable Object — e.g. N posts per minute per IP/author, stored in DO storage, returning 429 with Retry-After — and on cap overflow either reject with 429 or return an explicit eviction notice/count instead of silently slicing. This in-DO option is Free-tier-legal per the source comments (SQLite-backed DO is the only kind the Workers Free plan can create, single-threaded/strongly consistent). The candidate's alternative claim that Cloudflare Rate Limiting rules may need a paid plan for the needed granularity could NOT be verified from any comment in features/groupchat/ (grep found no mention of Rate Limiting/WAF/paid plan) — treat it as needing a check, do not rely on it; prefer the in-DO counter.

local: Grep the handler for any rate/counter/429 code and re-read lines 199-234 after the fix; unit-test the DO handler with >N rapid user posts from one IP and assert 429s and that seq/messages 1..k are retained, plus a second IP is unaffected.
deployment: With GROUPCHAT_TOKEN set, send a small bounded burst (e.g. 10-20 posts, not 200) from one IP, confirm 429 after the limit and no eviction of earlier messages, then POST /thread/reset {confirm:true} and confirm GET /thread returns seq 0; separately confirm a sustained-burst quota check is not needed — the limit, not the quota, is the control.
